entire_current.source_text: Proof of the $(1,\infty)$ case (used in Module 9): $|\sum_iu_iv_i|\le\sum_i|u_i||v_i|\le\max_j|v_j|\sum_i|u_i|$. The general case follows from Young's inequality $ab\le a^p/p+b^q/q$ (see Further Reading). Example: $w=(2,-1,3)$, $\varepsilon=0.1$: $w^\top\delta$ ranges over $\pm0.6$ on the $\ell_\infty$ ball, $\pm0.374$ on the $\ell_2$ ball, $\pm0.3$ on the $\ell_1$ ball. Since the box $[-1,1]^n$ is the $\ell_\infty$ unit ball, the hyperplane $w^\top a=b$ meets it iff $|b|\le\|w\|_1$.

Definition — Induced (operator) norm
    
      For $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ with input norm $\|\cdot\|_a$ and output norm $\|\cdot\|_b$: $\ \|A\|_{a\to b}=\max_{x\ne0}\|Ax\|_b/\|x\|_a=\max_{\|x\|_a=1}\|Ax\|_b$. It is the smallest constant with $\|Ax\|_b\le\|A\|_{a\to b}\|x\|_a$ for all $x$. We write $\|A\|_p$ when $a=b=p$; Module 13 writes $\|W\|_{p,\infty}$ for input $\ell_p$, output $\ell_\infty$.

Theorem — Submultiplicativity and the product bound
    
      $\|AB\|\le\|A\|\,\|B\|$ for induced norms (and for $\|\cdot\|_F$), since $\|ABx\|\le\|A\|\,\|Bx\|\le\|A\|\,\|B\|\,\|x\|$. Hence $\|A^k\|\le\|A\|^k$, and a network $W_l\phi(\cdots\phi(W_0x))$ with 1-Lipschitz activations is $\prod_k\|W_k\|_2$-Lipschitz.

Theorem — Submultiplicativity and the product bound
    
      $\|AB\|\le\|A\|\,\|B\|$ for induced norms (and for $\|\cdot\|_F$), since $\|ABx\|\le\|A\|\,\|Bx\|\le\|A\|\,\|B\|\,\|x\|$. Hence $\|A^k\|\le\|A\|^k$ for induced norms and every integer $k\ge0$; the same bound for the Frobenius norm holds for $k\ge1$. A network $W_l\phi(\cdots\phi(W_0x))$ with 1-Lipschitz activations is $\prod_k\|W_k\|_2$-Lipschitz.

individual_wording_decisions.reason: The support radius for weights (2,-1,3) and radius 1/10 is exactly sqrt(14)/10. Actual Holder23 proves strict .3735 and .3745 rounding bounds and that this value exceeds .374; the approximate decimal is now qualified without changing the other norm endpoints.

Input dimension n>=1 supplies a nonzero input and a nonempty unit sphere. Finite-dimensional compactness yields both actual maxima and the least among all real bound constants. For n=0 every real constant bounds the zero map and the literal maximum over nonzero inputs is empty. Output dimension may be zero.

Compatible induced norms obey submultiplicativity and every nonnegative integer power, including the zero-dimensional case. Frobenius submultiplicativity gives every positive power. Its zero power is the identity with norm sqrt(n); the actual Fin2 zero-matrix countermodel has identity norm sqrt(2)>1. The proposed phrase makes this distinction explicit.
